end.summary:
Practised multiplying by 10, 100, and 1000 using place value and zeros.
Worked through 25 × 36 by breaking 36 into 30 and 6.
Used doubling and halving examples, but doubled both factors instead of doubling one and halving the other.
Estimation was introduced but not completed; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Sameer practised place-value multiplication and explained why multiplying by 10, 100, or 1000 adds zeros. Breaking 25 × 36 into 25 × 30 and 25 × 6 worked well as a method. In the doubling-and-halving method, they doubled both numbers; this mix-up was still present at the end of the lesson. At home, practise a few examples by doubling one factor while halving the other, such as 25 × 16 = 50 × 8, and ask Sameer to explain what happens to the product.
